titles: 15 Ways We Listened to Music in the 1960s That Kids Can't Imagine
15 Things About 1960s Music Only People Over 60 Remember
Before Streaming: 15 Ways Music Filled Our Homes in the 1960s
description_intro:
This is 1960s music nostalgia the way we lived it: stacking 45s on the record changer, counting out coins at the record counter, and pressing those chrome push buttons on the AM car radio while Dad claimed his station.

We'll visit the glass listening booth, the jukebox at the diner, the record club by mail, the eight-track that went ka-chunk, and the family hi-fi console nobody was allowed to touch. And at number one, the little secret almost all of us kept after Mom switched off the light. Did our parents really never know?

Which one brought back a song you haven't hummed in years? Tell us where you grew up in the comments.

Warm amber lamplight, moonlit curtains, bottom quarter plain quilt.
